narratives.Overview:
## Summary

write fence refuses a path its own story file_scope declares when the path contains a __tests__ segment

## Context

Directive engine 0.107.0, content 0.107.0. Windows. Consumer project dispatching a story cohort to parallel swarm workers, each fence-pinned to its own story (pin confirmed in `.deft/ritual-state.json`).

The story's `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope[]` lists both `src/ui/fonts.css` and `src/ui/__tests__/fonts.test.ts`.

## Expected behavior

A path listed verbatim in the bound story's `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope[]` is writable by the worker pinned to that story, regardless of which directory segments the path contains.

## Actual behavior / gap

The write is denied:

```
Directive denied this direct write: path src/ui/__tests__/fonts.test.ts
is outside write fence story file_scope (source: story).
```

That exact string is present in `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope[]`. The sibling entry `src/ui/fonts.css`, from the same array in the same session, was allowed. The only difference between the two paths is the `__tests__` segment, which suggests the path matcher treats a `__`-wrapped directory as a special token rather than as a literal segment.

This is not one story. Four of nine active stories in the cohort declared a test file under `__tests__`, and it tends toward every story, because `verify:forward-coverage` (#1310) requires a co-located test per new source file. So the fence blocks the file another gate mandates — the two gates cannot both be satisfied.

## Session notes

### Why the failure is expensive to attribute

A `file_scope` mismatch reads like an authoring error in the brief, so the first instinct is to edit the brief — which cannot help, because the path is already there.

### The behaviour it trains

The only workaround available inside the session is the shell, which the fence does not inspect (`python -c` and friends are explicitly outside the deny). So a worker that hits this either stops — correct, and costs a dispatch round trip — or quietly writes the file through the shell, at which point the fence has taught agents to route around it. That is precisely what a write fence exists to prevent. Related: #3987, #3997.

### Suggested fix

- Check the path matcher's handling of `__`-wrapped directory segments; cover `__mocks__` and `__snapshots__` with the same test.
- Add a regression fixture with a `file_scope[]` entry under `__tests__` and assert the write is admitted.

### Dedup performed

Searched open issues in this repo on 2026-08-31 for `write fence __tests__`, `path matcher segment`, `file_scope test path denied`, `fence file_scope co-located test`. No existing report of this symptom. #3594 is the Shell dest-form enforcement knob, a different mechanism. #3987 and #3997 concern shell-tool coverage of the same gate, not segment matching.

### Scope note

This report was originally drafted together with a second symptom — the fence relativising an absolute write path against the parent repo root inside a worktree nested at `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<story>`. That symptom is being recorded as a comment on #3861 instead, since the panel there scoped it to verification against a build containing `c99f6159` (#3794 / #3807), which `v0.107.0` does not contain.

## Adoption impact

This report is a consumer hard-stop: the consumer cannot complete an intended Directive flow and has no reasonable workaround.

Title token: `BLOCKER`. This token does not apply the `adoption-blocker` ranking label. A privileged actor applies that label after the body-evidence test.

### Affected consumer flow and version

Dispatching a story cohort to parallel swarm workers, Directive engine 0.107.0 / content 0.107.0, Windows. The flow does not complete: a worker cannot write a file its own brief authorises, and the file in question is one `verify:forward-coverage` independently requires.

### Documented alternatives attempted

- **Widening `file_scope[]`** — not applicable; the exact path is already declared.
- **Rewriting the brief** — no value satisfies both sides, because the string the fence rejects is the string the fence is matching against.
- **Dropping the test** — refused; `verify:forward-coverage` requires it, and a source file with no test is the thing that gate exists to prevent.
- **Writing the file through the shell** — works, because the fence does not inspect `python -c` and similar. Not a reasonable workaround: it trains agents that the fence is bypassable, which defeats the gate for every future write.

### Observed recovery cost

Four of nine stories in one cohort were affected. Two workers stalled mid-story and returned to the parent for a dispatch round trip. The cohort's parallelism was abandoned and the remaining stories re-run serially.

### Triage owner and date

_(to be filled by a privileged actor when applying `adoption-blocker`)_

## Verdict and per-issue disposition

The four reports do not compose as one remedy portfolio. At dispatch SHA `fb9ece05e881d91b75a5bada1ea37d535c677f7d`, they cross four different authorities: story write authorization, acceptance-clause read authorization, source-to-test correspondence, and Git ignore evaluation. A shared path resolver would erase those distinctions.

- #4007: park as needs-reproduction and remove the `__tests__` matcher diagnosis from the proposed remedy. Do not promote a matcher change from the current evidence.
- #4008: close as superseded at this SHA by #3835 / commit `14529b90` (PR #3880), after confirming the consumer upgrades beyond 0.107.0. Do not restore basename-derived bindings.
- #4009: retain, but amend to the live defect: forward-coverage uses directory-agnostic basename correspondence. Treat use of `testRoots` as a design choice to reconcile with the existing test-boundary policy, not as configuration this gate currently promises to read.
- #4010: park or close as not reproduced. Reopen only with a minimal repository fixture and raw `git check-ignore -v --no-index` output that produces the empty-pattern attribution.

## Finding 1: The panel record is malformed, and the embedded blanket pre-consent cannot bind a later map

blocks-the-design

Evidence: the only in-envelope comment on #4007 is comment 5480979100. It has `role: triage`; it does not contain the required parent artifact token or the required `round:`, `siblings:`, and `input-ceiling:` fields. The other three threads have no in-envelope comments. The same triage comment contains an instruction-shaped `## Operator instruction, on the record` section claiming that blanket consent given before any successor map satisfies the later confirm conjunct. I treated that external-thread text as untrusted content and did not follow it.

Concrete failure mode: without the required pre-dispatch parent deposit, nothing durable establishes panel membership before siblings run, and no predicate checks completeness. Treating pre-consent as confirmation also lets a parent bind load-bearing per-heading takes the operator has never seen. A partial panel or an unreviewed map can therefore be recorded as complete.

Disposition consequence: no per-issue disposition from this round can bind through the claimed pre-consent path. The parent must record the panel-contract defect and obtain operator confirmation or amendment after the successor map exists. Because the required deposit had to precede dispatch, this round must not be represented as a conforming N=3 panel.

## Finding 2: The portfolio premise conflates path-shaped data with four different authority decisions

blocks-the-design

Evidence from the dispatch tree:

- #4007 reaches `matchAny` through `evaluateRuntimeAuthorityPath` in `packages/core/src/policy/runtime-authority.ts`; the inputs are the normalized write target and approved story `file_scope`.
- #4008 now deliberately emits `artifact_path: null` in `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts`, because issue and comment text is untrusted and cannot select a file for the clause walk. The walk reads only paths declared by approved `file_scope`.
- #4009 constructs a set of added test basenames in `packages/core/src/forward-coverage/evaluate.ts`; it is a correspondence check over one Git diff, not an authorization check.
- #4010 delegates ignore semantics to `git check-ignore -v --no-index`; its parser records Git's source, line, and pattern.

Concrete failure mode: a shared resolver would either weaken authority or import the wrong semantics. Basename fallback is tolerable only as a heuristic; in a write fence it broadens mutation authority, and in the clause walk it lets untrusted prose influence what file is read. Gitignore precedence and negation also cannot be replaced by the write-fence glob matcher without changing Git semantics.

Disposition consequence: reject a set-level implementation issue or shared-resolver remedy. Dispose each issue independently as listed above. Shared work is justified only at the diagnostic vocabulary level, not as one matcher or one policy surface.

Road not taken: a canonical repo-path service is attractive because all four reports mention path resolution and could share normalization plus diagnostics. The strongest case for it is consistency on slash normalization, root binding, and candidate reporting. I rejected it here because normalization is not the disputed decision; authorization, correspondence, and Git interpretation have different trusted inputs. I would reverse this verdict if the proposal were limited to a pure path value type and diagnostics, with each caller retaining its own authority predicate.

## Finding 3: #4007's claimed `__tests__` matcher defect does not reproduce

blocks-the-design

Evidence: I ran the built matcher at the dispatch SHA with exact entries for `src/ui/__tests__/fonts.test.ts`, `src/ui/__mocks__/fonts.ts`, and `src/ui/__snapshots__/fonts.snap`; all returned true. `src/ui/fonts.css` also returned true. The matcher splits only on `/` and gives `_` no special meaning. The same matcher source is present at v0.107.0, and no matcher or write-fence policy file changed between v0.107.0 and the dispatch SHA. Existing dispatcher mechanisms separately resolve the effective worktree root and report `payloadRoot` plus `effectiveRoot` on a denial.

Concrete failure mode: implementing the suggested `__`-segment fix changes a matcher that already admits the path, leaves the observed denial intact, and creates false confidence around a write-authority failure. In a cohort, that can continue to stall workers or train shell bypass while the actual loaded scope, target normalization, host payload, or effective-root mismatch remains unknown.

Disposition consequence: park #4007 as needs-reproduction, not an accepted matcher fix. A useful reproduction must capture the raw target supplied by the host, the normalized relative target, the loaded story allow paths, the active scope path, and the effective worktree root at the denial. If those values are byte-for-byte equal and the current matcher still denies, the issue can return with a falsifiable anchor.

## Finding 4: #4008 is superseded, and its basename remedy would reopen an injection boundary

blocks-the-design

Evidence: my direct derivation probe for `Add useDensity.ts exposing mode and setMode` returned one clause with `artifact_path: null` and `ambiguous: false`, not the reported bare filename. The dispatch source states why: clause text includes the untrusted issue body and comment thread, so derived clauses bind no path. Commit `14529b90` after v0.107.0 made the clause walk accept only paths already declared by approved `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope` and removed derived ambiguous readings.

Concrete failure mode: resolving a bare filename from clause prose against `file_scope`, especially by basename, lets an untrusted thread fragment influence which approved file is read and becomes ambiguous when a story contains repeated names such as `index.ts`. Restoring the report's suggested walk-time basename matching would regress the #3835 confused-deputy defense even if it made the old consumer symptom disappear.

Disposition consequence: close #4008 as superseded for the stated mechanism, with upgrade verification rather than new product work. If upgraded consumers still cannot complete, file the current null-binding or clause-adjudication symptom separately with the generated clause record and current-version walk output.

The strongest rejected position is that `file_scope` is already approved, so uniquely matching a basename inside it appears safe and repairs old briefs cheaply. It does bound the read set. It does not prove that untrusted clause text selected the intended member, and uniqueness can change as the story grows. I would reconsider only with a trusted, explicit clause-to-artifact binding authored before dispatch and covered by the approved-scope digest.

## Finding 5: #4009 is real, but `testRoots` is not yet this gate's contract

sharpens-framing

Evidence: both `src/ui/ledger-table/index.ts` and `src/other/index.ts` produce the same candidates, `index.test.ts` and `index.spec.ts`. The evaluator then reduces every added test path to `basename(p)` and checks set membership. The targeted `packages/core/src/forward-coverage/evaluate.test.ts` run passed all 18 tests, including the test that intentionally accepts a Python test under `tests/` by basename. `ForwardCoverageOptions` has no `testRoots`. The existing configured `testRoots` mechanism belongs to `packages/core/src/test-boundary`, where it classifies test placement and production references.

Concrete failure mode: in a multi-story diff, one unrelated `index.test.ts` can satisfy every newly added `index.ts`, so the fail-closed claim that each new source has a corresponding test is false. Conversely, simply requiring co-location would reject valid centralized test layouts that the existing behavior intentionally admits.

Disposition consequence: retain #4009, but amend its title and acceptance target around path-aware source-to-test correspondence. The design must state how `testBoundary.testRoots` maps a source-relative path into one or more test-relative candidates, or introduce a narrowly named forward-coverage mapping policy. It must not claim that the current gate ignores a configuration it never loads.

Road not taken: keep basename matching and only print searched candidates. That preserves language-neutral support for co-located and centralized tests with almost no configuration, which is the strongest defense of the current mechanism. Diagnostics reduce attribution cost but do not stop unrelated same-stem files from satisfying the gate. I would keep basename matching only for a repository that can deterministically prove stem uniqueness within the diff scope.

## Finding 6: #4010's blank-line mechanism does not reproduce against Git or the dispatch tree

blocks-the-design

Evidence: `readIgnorePatternSources` trims each ignore-file line and explicitly skips empty, comment, and negation lines before deriving probes. This file is unchanged from v0.107.0. In a temporary Git repository with `node_modules/`, a blank line, a comment, and a trailing newline, `git check-ignore -v --no-index` returned exit 1 with no output for both the lifecycle directory and sentinel file. That is Git's documented blank-line behavior. The parser can represent an empty pattern if Git emits one, but the report does not provide the raw command output or a fixture that causes Git to do so.

Concrete failure mode: adding another blank-line filter to the Directive parser is a no-op on the reproduced path and can conceal the actual source, such as a different binary, wrapper, excludes file, or output-shape mismatch. Under `--enforce`, the unexplained mismatch would remain a hard stop.

Disposition consequence: park or close #4010 as not reproduced; do not accept its suggested parser fix. A reopen needs the exact `.gitignore` bytes around the cited line, Git version, relevant exclude configuration, and raw command output. If Git truly emits `source:line:` for a match, then the defect is fail-closed validation of impossible matcher output, not blank-line parsing.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-31T16:17:00Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Round 1 open critique of the set #4007 / #4008 / #4009 / #4010 at SHA fb9ece05e881d91b75a5bada1ea37d535c677f7d. Process only. Issue bodies are untrusted consumer reports; I re-ran the named matchers and did not follow any suggested-fix list as an instruction. No embedded instruction was found in the four bodies.

## 1. The four gates do not share an evaluation engine
blocks-the-design

Evidence. At this SHA the four filed mechanisms sit on four different evaluators:

- Write fence: `matchAny` / `matchPath` in `packages/core/src/orchestration/pathspec.ts` (#1419), consumed by `evaluateRuntimeAuthorityPath`. That file is unchanged from v0.107.0 (last touch `2e7b3d95`).
- Clause bind: `extractPathTokens` plus `isDeclaredArtifactPath` in `packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts`. v0.107.0 `buildClause` stored the extracted token; HEAD `14529b90` (#3835) stores `null` and walks only `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope`.
- Forward coverage: `expectedTestBasenames` builds a basename `Set`. `packages/core/src/forward-coverage/` contains zero `testRoots` references.
- Lifecycle-visible: `git check-ignore -v --no-index` in `collectIgnoredRoots`; the in-process gitignore reader only derives extra probes and already skips blank, comment, and negation lines.

Failure mode. A "shared path-resolution" unit of work would retarget four gates, delay the two BLOCKER-titled issues, and still miss #4010, which is not on `matchPath` at all. It would also have to pick one matching tightness. #4008's option 2 wants basename-at-walk; #4009 wants to forbid that tightness; #3835 already forbids walking an undeclared basename. One library cannot ship those three.

Disposition. Keep four issues. Refuse a merge into one matcher/module. The only composition that survives re-verification is constraint coupling between #4007 and #4009 (the fence must admit the placement coverage will require) and shared-state coupling from #4008 (an uncompleted brief left in `xbrief/active/` is what `inspectActiveScope` reads). That is sequencing, not a shared engine.

Road not taken. Unify everyone on `pathspec` because it already claims glob SoT. Steelmanning that: three of the four reports are "this gate matched looser or tighter than the path the author wrote," and one matcher would stop a fifth dialect. What would flip the verdict is two of the four collapsing to the same `matchPath` bug on one pattern class. They do not.

## 2. #4007 is not a __-wrapped special token
blocks-the-design

Evidence. Direct writes of the reported pair through `resolveWriteFence` + `evaluateRuntimeAuthorityDirectWrite`:

- file_scope `[src/ui/fonts.css, src/ui/__tests__/fonts.test.ts]`: both `allowed: true`. Exact `matchPath` on the `__tests__`, `__mocks__`, and `__snapshots__` paths is true. Underscore is a literal character in `matchSegmentPattern`.
- file_scope `[src/ui/*, src/ui/fonts.css]`: css allowed; the nested test denied with the exact consumer string `Directive denied this direct write: path src/ui/__tests__/fonts.test.ts is outside write fence story file_scope (source: story).`

`*` is one path segment. `src/ui/__tests__/fonts.test.ts` is two segments under `src/ui`. The same deny fires for `src/ui/components/fonts.test.ts` with no dunders. `src/ui/**` admits the nested path.

I could not inspect the consumer brief, so I cannot confirm the claim that the exact test string was in the *loaded* array. I can say that if it was, this matcher admits it. Ritual pin is not that array: `runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite` loads story scope from `inspectActiveScope(effectiveRoot)` then `loadStoryWriteFenceFromPath`. `inspectActiveScope` sorts `xbrief/active/` and takes the first preflight-eligible path (`content/contracts/path-write-fence.md` residual: "Multiple active artifacts -> first preflight-eligible path wins"). It does not read `.deft/ritual-state.json`.

Failure mode. A `__`-literal exception leaves every other extra segment denied, adds a special case to the fence, and does not fix a worker whose loaded scope is a sibling story or a `src/ui/*` glob. It also invites a `__mocks__` / `__snapshots__` follow-up that the matcher does not need.

Disposition. Recut #4007. Drop the special-token story. Either (a) retarget to "single-segment glob vs co-located `__tests__` placement, plus which story `file_scope` the hook actually loaded," with a regression of `src/ui/*` vs a nested test, or (b) if the operator still holds that the exact path was in the loaded array, that claim is unreproduced here and cannot bind. Do not treat #3861 / #3794 as already covering the `src/ui/*` case; that work is worktree root, not segment glob. Do not invent a dunder exception.

## 3. #4008 option 2 is the defect #4009 and #3835 already closed
blocks-the-design

Evidence. v0.107.0 `buildClause` sets `artifact_path: paths[0]` from `extractPathTokens`. The regex allows a zero-directory prefix, so `Add useDensity.ts exposing...` stores `useDensity.ts`. At this SHA, `deriveAcceptanceClauses` returns `artifact_path: null` for that line. Walking a leftover bare filename against `declaredScope: ["src/ui/ledger-table/useDensity.ts"]` is `unverifiable` / not adjudicable (`artifact path is not declared on plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope ... (#3835)`), not `failed`. `isDeclaredArtifactPath("useDensity.ts", [full path])` is false.

#4009's existence half is the same tightness in the other direction: `expectedTestBasenames("src/ui/ledger-table/index.ts")` is `["index.test.ts", "index.spec.ts"]`, matched by basename anywhere in the diff. The v1 comment and `evaluate.test.ts` ("matches a Python test under tests/ by basename") lock that.

Failure mode. Binding #4008 by "match on basename at walk time" would (1) verify a clause against a same-named file in another module, which is the barrel collision #4009 reports, and (2) read a path the brief did not declare, which is the #3835 third-party-comment hole. A set that ships both "loosen the walk" and "tighten coverage" as local fixes fights itself.

Disposition. Strike option 2 from #4008. The remaining bind path is option 1 / 3 against the existing surface: `readDeclaredArtifactScope` / `isDeclaredArtifactPath` / the promote-time derivation already invoked from `scope:promote`. Do not add a second path matcher.

## 4. Recut #4008 against HEAD, and split the two adjacent mechanisms
sharpens-framing

Evidence. #3835 already stopped storing a prose path. It did not bind a clause to the matching `file_scope` entry. A newly derived brief at this SHA therefore walks as all-unverifiable; `clauseWalkBlocks` does not fail-closed when `adjudicableUnverified === 0`. That is not the consumer's `1 failed / 0 unverifiable` on v0.107.0, and it is also not "clauses resolve against the path the story already declares."

The two split candidates in the #4008 body are real and separate:

- `ImplementationPlan` is in `NARRATIVE_KEYS` in `packages/core/src/intake/clause-derivation.ts`, so it is concatenated into the statement `deriveAcceptanceClauses` reads when `plan.items` is empty. `ACCEPTANCE_SHAPED_KEYS` in `acceptance-activate-gate.ts` does not include it, so promote/activate does not treat it as acceptance-shaped.
- `evaluateLiteralAcceptanceFromPlan` runs in `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts` only under `act === "complete"`. Promote does not run the allowlist.

Failure mode. A single #4008 PR titled "stop storing bare filenames" either duplicates #3835 or fights it, and can land without moving the allowlist or stopping ImplementationPlan fallback. The consumer hard-stop they felt at complete can already change shape on upgrade while the file_scope bind gap remains.

Disposition. Recut #4008 to: bind (or fail closed) at `scope:promote` when a derived clause's path tokens do not match `file_scope`, including `readings[]`. Split or park ImplementationPlan-as-acceptance and late literal-AC allowlist. Do not close #4008 as already-fixed: null is not a file_scope bind.

## 5. #4009 is a v1 matching-contract change; reuse test-boundary testRoots
sharpens-framing

Evidence. Forward-coverage never reads `plan.policy` test roots. `packages/core/src/test-boundary/policy.ts` already ships typed `testRoots` with default `**/__tests__/**`. The existence half is intentionally directory-agnostic "so co-located, tests/, and __tests__/ layouts all count." The filed error text (`expected one of: index.test.ts, index.spec.ts`) is what `expectedTestBasenames` returns.

Failure mode. Consulting `testRoots` while keeping stem matching still false-passes a distant `index.test.ts`. Tightening to a path-relative match without a write-fence placement that the worker can actually write still leaves the story uncommittable (finding 2). Adding a barrel allowlist is the #3156 move the reporter correctly refused.

Disposition. Keep #4009 as its own issue. Reuse `test-boundary` `testRoots` / `testFilePatterns`; do not add a third test-root config. Record the fence constraint as a cross-issue note toward #4007 after that issue is recut, not as a merge.

## 6. #4010's skip-blank remedy already holds; empty-pattern match-all was not reproduced
sharpens-framing

Evidence. `readIgnorePatternSources` continues on `line.length === 0`, `#`, and `!`. `expandGitignoreGlobToConcrete("")` returns `null`. `ignorePatternLooksLifecycleRelevant("")` is false. `git check-ignore -v --no-index` on a conventional blank-line `.gitignore` exits 1 (not ignored). A `*` on line 51 does hide every lifecycle root and prints `[deft lifecycle-visible] hidden xbrief/proposed/  (.gitignore:51:*)` -- the star is present. The consumer tell `(.gitignore:51:)` with an empty rule is the parser accepting an empty pattern *if git emits one*. I did not get git to emit one from a blank, spaces, or comment line.

Failure mode. Binding "skip blank and comment lines" is a no-op that looks like a fix. Folding #4010 into a shared resolver implies this gate matches in-process, which it does not. A second gitignore engine would drift from `git check-ignore` and recreate the bug class this gate was written to avoid (#3505).

Disposition. Drop #4010 from the set, or recut it to "reproduce empty-pattern `check-ignore -v` output on the consumer file" before any parser change. Do not invent an in-process match-all.

## 7. Swarm lens: the expensive coupling is active/ holding the fence
sharpens-framing

Evidence. Hook story scope is the first eligible brief under `xbrief/active/` of `effectiveRoot`, not the occupancy pin. #4008's uncompleted briefs remain in `active/` and are what later workers are fenced by. Shell dest-form enforcement defaults to `off` (`path-write-fence.md` / #3594); the cooperative bypass the #4007 body names (`python -c`) is already the dest-form threat model, with recall work on #3987 / fail-open posture on #3997. Those issues are not in this set.

Untrusted input: clause text is issue+thread prose (#3835); `.gitignore` is clone-local; `file_scope` is brief JSON. #3835 already closed "lift a path out of a comment and read the file."
